'''Michael Sela''' ({{langx|he|מיכאל סלע}}; '''Mieczysław Salomonowicz'''; 2 March 1924 – 27 May 2022) was an Israeli [[immunologist]] of [[Polish Jewish]] origin. He was a president of [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in [[Rehovot]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=מסע הקסם המדעי - חדשות מדע, תגליות ומידע לציבור מבית מכון ויצמן למדע |url=https://heb.wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/ |access-date=28 May 2022 |website=מסע הקסם המדעי - חדשות מדע, תגליות ומידע לציבור מבית מכון ויצמן למדע |language=he}}</ref>

== Early life and academic career ==
Michael Sela was born as Mieczysław Salomonowicz in [[Tomaszów Mazowiecki]], Poland, on 2 March 1924.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.weizmann.ac.il/WeizmannCompass/sections/people-behind-the-science/prof-michael-sela |title=Prof. Michael Sela &#124; Still hard at work, pursuing the understanding of immunology &#124; WeizmannCompass |publisher=Weizmann.ac.il |date= 4 June 2017|access-date=10 February 2020}}</ref><ref name="autogeneratedil">{{cite web|url=https://in.bgu.ac.il/en/loeb/OHP/Pages/Michael_Sela.aspx |title=Oral History Project - Michael Sela |publisher=In.bgu.ac.il |access-date=21 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=USA |title=Isolation and Characterization of Antibodies: the Work of Michael Sela |journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry |volume=285 |issue=39 |pages=e12–e14 |publisher=Ncbi.nlm.nih.gov |date=6 May 2019 |pmc=2943276 |doi=10.1074/jbc.O110.000235 |doi-access=free }}</ref> In 1935 when he was 11 years old he and his family moved to [[Romania]].<ref name="autogeneratedil"/><ref>[https://docksci.com/historical-perspective-an-interview-with-renowned-immunologist-drmichael-sela_5a47dd62d64ab20b6693d9ed.html "Historical perspective: An interview with renowned Immunologist Dr. Michael Sela "]</ref> In 1941 when he was 17 years old he and his family immigrated to Mandatory Palestine.<ref name="autogeneratedil"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.weizmann.ac.il/WeizmannCompass/sections/people-behind-the-science/prof-michael-sela |title=Prof. Michael Sela &#124; Still hard at work, pursuing the understanding of immunology &#124; WeizmannCompass |publisher=Weizmann.ac.il |date= 4 June 2017|access-date=21 February 2020}}</ref> He studied at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] (M.Sc., Chemistry, 1946; Ph.D., 1954).<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1002/pro.5560070723 | title=Probing into the realm of proteins and immunity | date=1998 | last1=Sela | first1=Michael | journal=Protein Science | volume=7 | issue=7 | pages=1653–1659 | pmid=9684902 | pmc=2144067 }}</ref>

Sela was professor in the Weizmann Institute's Immunology Department. He was also a president of the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], from 1975 to 1985. He died in Rehovot on 27 May 2022 at the age of 98.<ref>{{cite journal | url = https://www.thelancet.com/pdfs/journals/lancet/PIIS0140-6736(22)01293-4.pdf | title = Obituary | journal = The Lancet| year = 2022 | volume = 400}}</ref>

== Research ==
Sela is known for his research in [[immunology]], particularly for research on synthetic [[antigen]]s,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1126/science.166.3911.1365|title = Antigenicity - some molecular aspects|last1 = Sela|first1 = M.|journal=Science|year=1969|volume = 166|number = 3911|pages = 1365–1374| pmid=4900368 | bibcode=1969Sci...166.1365S }}</ref> [[molecule]]s that trigger the [[immune system]] to attack. This work of Sela has led to the discovery of the genetic control of the immune response, as well as to the design of [[vaccine]]s based on synthetic molecules.

He was among the first who introduced the use of linear and branched synthetic [[polypeptide]]s as antigens, and this  brought about a better understanding of immunological phenomena.<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1084/jem.122.3.517|title = Genetic control of antibody response. 1. Demonstration of determinant-specific differences in response to synthetic polypeptide antigens in two strains of inbred mice|journal = J. Exp. Med.|volume = 122|number=3|pages = 517–531|year =1965|first1 = Hugh O.|last1 = McDevitt|first2 = Michael|last2 = Sela| pmid=5839284 | s2cid=16188026 |pmc = 2138070}}</ref>

For several decades, Sela was interested in the possibility of fighting the autoimmune disease, experimental allergic [[encephalomyelitis]]<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1073/pnas.94.20.10821|title = Copolymer 1 induces T cells of the T helper type 2 that crossreact with myelin basic protein and suppress experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis|last1 = Aharoni|first1= R|last2 = Teitelbaum|first2 = D|last3 =  Sela|first3 = M|last4 = Arnon|first4 = R|journal =Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA|volume=94|number=20|pages= 10821–10826|year=1997 | pmid=9380718 | pmc=23498 | bibcode=1997PNAS...9410821A | doi-access=free }}</ref> with synthetic analogs of the molecules in the [[myelin sheath]] of the brain which are capable of provoking the disease.

He is probably best known as the co-developer (with [[Ruth Arnon]] and [[Dvora Teitelbaum]]) of the [[multiple sclerosis]] drug [[copaxone]].<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1212/WNL.41.4.533|title = A placebo-controlled, double-blind, randomized, 2-center, pilot trial of COP 1 in chronic progressive multiple sclerosis|last1 =  Bornstein|first1 = M B |last2 = Miller|first2 = A |last3 =  Slagle|first3 = S |last4 =  Weitzman|first4 = M |last5 =  Drexler|first5 = E |last6= Keilson|first6= M |last7 =  Spada |first7 = V |last8 =   Weiss|first8 = W |last9 = Appel|first9 = S |last10 =  Rolak|first10 = L  |last11 =  Harati|first11 = Y |last12= Brown|first12 = S |last13 = Arnon|first13 = R |last14 = Jacobsohn|first14 = I |last15 = Teitelbaum|first15 = D |last16 = Sela|first16 = M |journal = Neurology|volume = 41|number=4|pages = 533–539|year=1991 | pmid=2011253 | s2cid=12602679 }}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
Sela received numerous major national and international awards:
* The [[Israel Prize]] in Life Sciences (1959)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashyag/Tashkab_Tashyag_Rikuz.htm?DictionaryKey=Tashyat |title=Israel Prize recipients in 1959 (in Hebrew) |publisher=Israel Prize Official Site |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120307203909/http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashyag/Tashkab_Tashyag_Rikuz.htm?DictionaryKey=Tashyat |archive-date=7 March 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* Germany's [[Otto Warburg Medal]] (1968)<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.otto-warburg-medaille.org/index.php/previous-award-winners.html|title= Otto-Warburg-Medal|publisher= GBM|access-date= 12 January 2014|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190107204548/http://www.otto-warburg-medaille.org/index.php/previous-award-winners.html|archive-date= 7 January 2019|url-status= dead}}</ref>
* The [[Rothschild Prize]] (1967)<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Rothschild Prize |url=https://www.yadhanadiv.org.il/the-rothschild-prize/ |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=Yad Hanadiv |language=en-US}}</ref>
*Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1971)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Michael Sela|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/michael-sela|access-date=20 December 2021|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref>
* Germany's [[Emil von Behring]] Prize (1972)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Auszeichnungen der UMR |url=https://www.uni-marburg.de/de/universitaet/profil/universitaetundgesellschaft/auszeichnungen |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=Philipps-Universität Marburg |language=de}}</ref>
*Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] of the United States (1976)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Michael Sela|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/michael-sela-x6ubcz/|access-date=20 December 2021|website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref>
* Canada's [[Gairdner Foundation International Award]] (1980)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Foundation |first=The Gairdner |title=Michael Sela - Gairdner Foundation Award Winner |url=https://www.gairdner.org/winner/michael-sela |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=The Gairdner Foundation |language=en}}</ref>
* France's Institut de la Vie Prize (1984)<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2022-05-28 |title=Renowned Israeli immunologist Michael Sela dies at 98 |url=https://www.jpost.com/j-spot/article-707935 |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=[[The Jerusalem Post]] |language=en |issn=0792-822X }}</ref>
* Germany's Commander's Cross of the [[Federal Cross of Merit|Order of Merit Award]] (1986)<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Report of the Committee for the Assessment of the State of Biomedical Research in Israel |url=https://www.academy.ac.il/SystemFiles/21690.pdf |website=The Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities}}</ref>
* France's Officier de l'Ordre de la [[Légion d'honneur]] (1987)<ref name=":1" />
* Member (Hon. causa) of The Romanian Academy ([[Academia Română]]) (1991)<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |url=http://www.acad.ro/membri_ar/membri.htm |title=Membrii Academiei Române |access-date=16 January 2017 |archive-date=29 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130729014349/http://acad.ro/membri_ar/membri.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* UNESCO's Albert Einstein Golden Medal (1995)<ref name=":2" />
*Member of the [[American Philosophical Society]] (1995)<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Michael+Sela&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=20 December 2021|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref>
* [[Interbrew-Baillet Latour Health Prize]] of Belgium (1997)<ref>{{Cite web |date=1997-04-13 |title=Belgian Queen to Present the Award - Weizmann Wonder Wander - News, Features and Discoveries |url=https://wis-wander.weizmann.ac.il/people/belgian-queen-present-award |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=Weizmann Wonder Wander - News, Features and Discoveries from the Weizmann Institute of Science |language=en}}</ref>
* The [[Wolf Prize in Medicine]] (1998), along with [[Ruth Arnon]], for "their major discoveries in the field of immunology".<ref>[http://www.wolffund.org.il/cat.asp?id=24&cat_title=MEDICINE The Wolf Prize in Medicine] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090226015735/http://www.wolffund.org.il/cat.asp?id=24&cat_title=MEDICINE |date=26 February 2009 }}</ref>
